full_judgment:
This Rule under section 115(1) of the Code of Civil Procedure was issued against the judgment and decree dated 17-1-2001 and 25-1-2001 respectively passed by the learned District Judge, Mymensingh in Family Appeal No. 34 of 2000 reversing the judgment and decree dated 30-3-2000 passed by the learned Senior Assistant Judge, Family Court, Sadar, Mymensingh in Family suit No.9 of 1999. 

 4. The family suit came up fur hearing before the Court of learned Senior Assistant Judge, Mymensingh and the plaintiff examined 2 witnesses to prove her case and the defendant No. 1 examined himself. After hearing the learned Advocates of the parties and considering the materials on record, the trial Court was pleased to dismiss the suit by her judgment and decree dated 30-3-2000 in Family Suit No.9 of 1999. 

 5. Against the said judgment and decree the plaintiff preferred an appeal before the Court of learned District Judge, Mymensingh which was marked and numbered as Family Appeal No. 34 of 2000. 

 6. After hearing the learned Advocates of the parties and considering the materials on record the learned District Judge, Mymensingh was pleased to allow the appeal and set aside the judgment and decree of the trial Court and decreed the suit. 

 "There is a great difference between a marriage which is void ab initio (batil) and one which is invalid (Fasid), If a man were to contract a marriage with a woman related to him within the prohibited decrees the marriage would be void ab initio........... and invalid marriage is one where the parties are not liable under an inherent capacity or absolute bar, or where the disability is such as can be removed at any time. The issues of such unions are legitimate. " 

 14. Both the Courts below considered the reported case of Abdul Gani and others vs Bibi and others reported in PLD 1962 (WP) Lahore 531 giving the opinion of Abu Yusuf and Mohammad observing in Mohammedan Law by Syed Amir Ali (5th Edition 202) holding that: there is a great difference between a marriage which is void ab initio (Batil) and one which is invalid (Fasid). If a man were to contract a marriage with a woman related to him within the prohibited decrees the marriage would be void ab initio. An invalid marriage is one where the parties are not liable under an inherent capacity or absolute bar, or where the disability is such as can be removed at any time. The issues of such unions are legitimate.
